policies.policy_title: Freeze non-essential immigration
policies.stated: Reform UK will freeze all non-essential immigration, with the exception of essential skills in healthcare, to relieve pressure on housing and public services, and increase wages.

source.quote: Freeze Non-Essential Immigration Strict limits on immigration are the only way to relieve the pressure on our housing, public services, increase wages and protect our culture, identity and values. Essential skills, mainly around healthcare, must be the only exception.

policies.policy_title: Detain and deport illegal migrants
policies.stated: Reform UK will detain and deport illegal migrants, including picking them up in small boats and returning them to France, leaving the ECHR, prohibiting resettlement, and barring asylum or citizenship claims for those entering from safe countries. A new Department of Immigration will be created with no legal aid for non-citizens.

source.quote: Stop the Boats with our 4 Point Plan Leave the European Convention on Human Rights. Zero illegal immigrants to be resettled in the UK. New Department of Immigration. Pick up illegal migrants out of boats and take them back to France. Secure Detention for all Illegal Migrants All asylum seekers that arrive illegally from safe countries will be processed rapidly, offshore if necessary. Those entering from a safe country will also be barred from claiming asylum or citizenship. No legal aid for non-citizens. Those rejected will be returned.

policies.policy_title: Impose an Employer Immigration Tax
policies.stated: Reform UK will raise the National Insurance rate to 20% for foreign workers, exempting essential foreign health and care workers and businesses with 5 or fewer staff, to incentivise employing British citizens and boost wages.

source.quote: Employer Immigration Tax The National Insurance rate will be raised to 20% for foreign workers. This would incentivise businesses to employ British citizens whose National Insurance rate would stay at 13.8%. Essential foreign health and care workers would be exempt from the tax, as would businesses who employ 5 staff members and under.

policies.policy_title: Restrict international student visas
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce new visa rules barring dependents for international students, allowing only those with essential skills to remain in the UK, and closing down fake courses and immigration schemes.

source.quote: Bar Student Dependents Introduce new visa rules for international students that bar dependents. Only international students with essential skills can remain in the UK. Close down fake courses and immigration schemes that abuse the rules.

policies.policy_title: Impose 5-year residency and employment requirement for benefits
policies.stated: Reform UK will require 5 years of residency and employment to claim any benefits in the UK, aiming to stop health tourism and immediate access to welfare.

source.quote: Stop Health Tourism and Immediate Access to Benefits We will impose a requirement of 5 years residency and employment to claim any benefits in the UK.

policies.policy_title: Immediate deportation for foreign criminals
policies.stated: Reform UK will immediately deport foreign nationals after their prison sentence ends and withdraw citizenship from immigrants who commit crimes, with exceptions for minor misdemeanours.

source.quote: Immediate Deportation for Foreign Criminals Deport foreign nationals immediately after their prison sentence ends. Withdraw citizenship from immigrants who commit crime with the exception of some misdemeanour offences.

policies.policy_title: Halt interest payments on QE reserves
policies.stated: Reform UK will stop the Bank of England from paying interest to commercial banks on Quantitative Easing (QE) reserves, which they project would save around £35 billion per year.

source.quote: Bank of England Must Stop Paying Interest to Commercial Banks on QE Reserves This approach would save around £35 billion per year and has been endorsed by senior figures at the Financial Times, New Economics Foundation, and IFS, as well as two former Deputy Governors of the Bank of England.

policies.policy_title: Mandate 5% departmental spending cuts
policies.stated: Reform UK will require every government department to cut wasteful spending, bureaucracy, and improve efficiency by 5%, aiming to save £50 billion per year without affecting frontline services.

source.quote: Save £5 in every £100 Every department must slash wasteful spending, cut bureaucracy, improve efficiency and negotiate better value procurement without touching frontline services. This will save £50 billion per year, ensure tax cuts and boost our economy.

policies.policy_title: Cut foreign aid by 50%
policies.stated: Reform UK will cut the foreign aid budget by 50%, saving £6 billion, and undertake a major review of its effectiveness, including payments to global quangos.

source.quote: Cut Foreign Aid by 50% Save £6 billion from the £12.8 billion budget. A major review is needed into the effectiveness of overseas aid. That includes global quangos to which we pay over £7 billion every year.

policies.policy_title: Improve HMRC tax collection
policies.stated: Reform UK will improve HMRC's competence to collect tens of billions in unpaid taxes, which they attribute to understaffing and bad management.

source.quote: Collect £ Billions in Unpaid Tax HM Revenue and Customs failed to collect tens of billions in taxes last year due to understaffing and bad management. Improved HMRC competence would deliver lower taxes to British workers.

policies.policy_title: Raise income tax threshold to £20,000
policies.stated: Reform UK will lift the income tax starting threshold to £20,000, which they state will take 7 million people out of income tax and save every worker almost £1,500 per year. The higher rate threshold will be raised to £70,000.

source.quote: Make Work Pay. Lift the Income Tax Start Point to £20,000 Per Year This frees up to 7 million people from paying Income Tax and saves every worker almost £1,500 per year. Basic Tax rate stays at 20%. The higher rate should begin at £70,000.

policies.policy_title: Cut energy taxes
policies.stated: Reform UK will cut energy taxes by lowering fuel duty by 20p per litre, scrapping VAT on energy bills, and scrapping environmental levies, which they state will save households over £500 per year.

source.quote: Cut Energy Taxes, Beat the Cost-of-Living Crisis Save households over £500 per year. Lower fuel duty by 20p per litre for both residential and business users. Scrap VAT on energy bills. Scrap environmental levies.

policies.policy_title: Cut residential stamp duty
policies.stated: Reform UK will cut residential stamp duty to 0% below £750,000, 2% from £750,000-£1.5 million, and 4% over £1.5 million, aiming to boost economic activity and housebuilding.

source.quote: Cut Residential Stamp Duty Substantially boost economic activity and housebuilding by cutting Stamp Duty to 0% below £750k. Cut it to 2% from £750k - £1.5m and cut it to 4% over £1.5m.

policies.policy_title: Abolish VAT tourist tax
policies.stated: Reform UK will abolish the VAT refund scheme for tourist shopping, which they claim has cost the economy over £10 billion and deterred up to 2 million tourists.

source.quote: Abolish the VAT Tourist Tax The government has cost our economy over £10 billion when they stopped the VAT refund scheme for tourist shopping. This also deterred up to 2 million tourists.

policies.policy_title: Abolish inheritance tax for estates under £2 million
policies.stated: Reform UK will abolish Inheritance Tax (IHT) for all estates under £2 million, covering approximately 98% of estates, with a 20% tax rate above £2 million and an option to donate to charity instead.

source.quote: Abolish Inheritance Tax (IHT) for all Estates Under £2m That means some 98% of all estates. The rate above £2m will be 20% tax, with the option to donate to charity instead.

policies.policy_title: Reduce Corporation Tax and raise profit threshold
policies.stated: Reform UK will free over 1.2 million Small and Medium Sized Businesses (SMEs) from Corporation Tax by lifting the minimum profit threshold to £100,000, and reduce the main Corporation Tax rate from 25% to 20%, then to 15% from Year 3.

source.quote: Free Over 1.2 Million Small and Medium Sized Businesses from Corporation Tax Lift the minimum profit threshold to £100k. Reduce the main Corporation Tax Rate from 25% to 20%, then to 15% from Year 3.

policies.policy_title: Abolish IR35 rules
policies.stated: Reform UK will abolish IR35 rules to support sole traders, acknowledging that self-employed individuals often work longer hours and take more risks without pension or sick pay benefits.

source.quote: Abolish IR35 Rules to Support Sole Traders Britain’s self-employed often work longer hours and take more risks. Many have no pension and receive no sick pay.

policies.policy_title: Abolish Business Rates for high street SMEs and introduce Online Delivery Tax
policies.stated: Reform UK will abolish Business Rates for high street-based Small and Medium Sized Enterprises (SMEs), offsetting this with a 4% Online Delivery Tax for large, multinational enterprises to create a fairer playing field. They will also cut entrepreneurs' tax to 5%.

source.quote: Abolish Business Rates for high street based SMEs. Offset this with Online Delivery Tax at 4% for large, multinational enterprises to create a fairer playing field for high streets. Cut entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.

policies.policy_title: Lift the VAT threshold to £150,000
policies.stated: Reform UK will lift the VAT threshold to £150,000 to free up small entrepreneurs from red tape.

source.quote: Lift the VAT Threshold to £150,000 Free up small entrepreneurs from red tape.

policies.policy_title: Reform the planning system to fast-track housing and infrastructure on brownfield sites
policies.stated: Reform UK will reform the planning system to fast-track new housing on brownfield sites and infrastructure projects, particularly in coastal regeneration areas, Wales, the North, and the Midlands. This includes fast-tracking planning and tax incentives for brownfield site development, implementing 'loose fit planning' for large residential developments with pre-approved guidelines.

source.quote: Reform the Planning System Fast-track new housing on brownfield sites and infrastructure projects to boost businesses, especially in coastal regeneration areas, Wales, the North, and the Midlands. Review the Planning System Fast-track planning and tax incentives for development of brownfield sites. ‘Loose fit planning’ policy for large residential developments with preapproved guidelines and developer requirements.

consolidated_from: Reform the planning system to fast-track housing and infrastructure on brownfield sites
Review the planning system for brownfield development

policies.policy_title: Slash red tape for businesses
policies.stated: Reform UK will scrap thousands of laws, including employment laws, that they claim hold back British business and damage productivity, to make it easier to hire and fire staff.

source.quote: Slash Red Tape to Boost Industry and Exports Scrap thousands of laws that hold back British business and damage productivity, including employment laws. We must make it easier to hire and fire so that businesses can grow.

policies.policy_title: Simplify the tax system
policies.stated: Reform UK will undertake a major simplification of the UK's tax code, citing its current complexity of over 21,000 pages.

source.quote: Reform the Tax System Major simplification is needed. At over 21,000 pages, the UK’s tax code is a burden. Hong Kong’s tax code is under 500 pages.

policies.policy_title: Address NHS doctor and nurse shortages
policies.stated: Reform UK will tackle NHS and social care staffing shortages by making all frontline staff pay zero basic rate tax for three years, ending training caps for UK medical students, and writing off student fees pro rata over 10 years of NHS service.

source.quote: End Doctor and Nurse Shortages All frontline NHS and social care staff to pay zero basic rate tax for 3 years. This will help retain existing staff and attract many who have left to return. End training caps for all UK medical students. Write off student fees pro rata per year over 10 years of NHS service for all doctors, nurses and medical staff.

policies.policy_title: Increase use of independent healthcare capacity
policies.stated: Reform UK will harness independent and not-for-profit health provision in the UK and overseas, and offer tax relief of 20% on all private healthcare and insurance, aiming to relieve pressure on the NHS and improve care for all.

source.quote: Use Independent Healthcare Capacity We will harness independent and not-for-profit health provision in the UK and overseas. Tax Relief of 20% on all Private Healthcare and Insurance This will improve care for all by relieving pressure on the NHS. Those who rely on the NHS will enjoy faster, better care. Independent healthcare capacity will grow rapidly, providing competition and reducing costs.

policies.policy_title: Introduce NHS voucher scheme for waiting lists
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce an NHS voucher scheme where patients receive a voucher for private treatment if they cannot see a GP within 3 days, a consultant within 3 weeks, or have an operation within 9 weeks. Services will remain free at the point of use.

source.quote: Put Patients in Charge With a New NHS Voucher Scheme NHS Patients will receive a voucher for private treatment if they can’t see a GP within 3 days. For a consultant it would be 3 weeks. For an operation, 9 weeks. Services will always be free at the point of use.

policies.policy_title: Improve NHS efficiency and cut waste
policies.stated: Reform UK will improve NHS efficiency by opening operating theatres on weekends, planning rotas further in advance, negotiating better procurement prices, reviewing Private Finance Contracts, charging those who fail to attend appointments without notice, and abolishing the NHS Race and Health Observatory.

source.quote: Improve Efficiency. Cut Waste and Unnecessary Managers Operating theatres must be open on weekends. Rotas must be planned further in advance. Nail down better prices using economies of scale. Review all NHS Private Finance Contracts for significant savings potential. Charge those who fail to attend medical appointments without notice. Abolish the NHS Race and Health Observatory.

policies.policy_title: Reduce A&E waiting times with 'Pharmacy First' and tax incentives
policies.stated: Reform UK will cut A&E waiting times through a 'Pharmacy First, GP Second, A&E Last' campaign, and offer tax incentives for new pharmacies and those employing more staff.

source.quote: Save A&E Cut waiting times with a campaign of ‘Pharmacy First, GP Second, A&E Last’. We will offer tax incentives for new pharmacies and those who employ more staff to assist in relieving pressure on A&E.

policies.policy_title: Launch public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms
policies.stated: Reform UK will launch a Public Inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms, noting that excess deaths are nearly as high as during the Covid pandemic and young people are over-represented.

source.quote: Excess Deaths and Vaccine Harms Public Inquiry Excess deaths are nearly as high as they were during the Covid pandemic. Young people are over-represented.

policies.policy_title: Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies
policies.stated: Reform UK will scrap Net Zero targets and associated subsidies, projecting savings of over £30 billion per year for the public sector. They will also scrap £10 billion of renewable energy subsidies through equivalent taxes.

source.quote: Scrap Net Zero and Related Subsidies Ditching Net Zero could save the public sector over £30 billion per year for the next 25 years. Scrap Annual £10 Billion of Renewable Energy Subsidies Achieve this through equivalent taxes on them.

policies.policy_title: Unlock North Sea oil, gas, and shale reserves
policies.stated: Reform UK will fast-track licences for North Sea gas and oil, and grant shale gas licences on test sites for two years to enable major production once safety is proven, with local compensation schemes. This also includes fast-tracking licences for new oil and gas exploration in the North Sea to strengthen the UK's energy security and reduce reliance on imports.

source.quote: Cheap, Secure Energy for Britain Start fast-track licences of North Sea gas and oil. Grant shale gas licences on test sites for 2 years. Enable major production when safety is proven, with local compensation schemes. UK energy security remains vital, which is why Reform UK will fast-track new oil and gas exploration in the North Sea. This will also ensure a transition to new technologies that are proven to cut emissions, rather than damaging the economy to achieve unaffordable targets.

consolidated_from: Unlock North Sea oil, gas, and shale reserves
Fast-track licences for new oil and gas exploration in the North Sea

policies.policy_title: Accelerate development of cleaner energy technologies
policies.stated: Reform UK will fast-track clean nuclear energy with new Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) built in Britain, and increase incentivised ethical UK lithium mining, combined cycle gas turbines, clean synthetic fuel, tidal power, and explore clean coal mining.

source.quote: Cleaner Energy from New Technology Fast-track clean nuclear energy with new Small Modular Reactors, built in Britain. Increase and incentivise ethical UK lithium mining for electric batteries, combined cycle gas turbines, clean synthetic fuel, tidal power and explore clean coal mining.

policies.policy_title: Increase police numbers by 40,000
policies.stated: Reform UK will commence recruitment to increase UK per capita police numbers to 300 per 100,000 population, adding 40,000 new front-line officers over a five-year parliament.

source.quote: Commence Increase in Police Numbers Recruitment to increase UK per capita police numbers to 300 per 100k population. That is 40,000 new front-line officers, over a 5-year parliament.

policies.policy_title: Implement zero-tolerance policing
policies.stated: Reform UK will implement zero-tolerance policing, clamping down on all crime and antisocial behaviour, substantially increasing Stop and Search, mandating prison for violent crimes and knife possession, and imposing mandatory life imprisonment for drug dealing and trafficking. A new offence of Substantial Possession of Drugs will carry heavy fines.

source.quote: Commence Zero Tolerance Policing Clampdown on all crime and antisocial behaviour. Increase Stop and Search substantially. Prison for violent crimes and possessing a knife. Drug dealing and trafficking will get mandatory life imprisonment. A new offence of Substantial Possession of Drugs will meet heavy fines.

policies.policy_title: Reform police leadership and recruitment
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce a new police leadership and recruitment regime with a strong preference for ex-military officers, high standards of fitness and presentation, and the power to sack Chief Constables who allow 'two-tier policing.' They will also de-politicise the College of Policing, replace degree-standard entry with an entrance exam, require a 2-year probationary period, and implement stricter entry requirements.

source.quote: New Police Leadership and Recruitment Regime Strong preference for ex-military officers and personnel. High standards of fitness and presentation for front line officers. Sack Chief Constables that allow two-tier policing. De-Politicise the College of Policing Prioritise crime prevention, discipline, public service and high standards of strength and fitness among trainees. Replace degree-standard entry with an entrance exam. Require officers to complete a 2-year probationary period. Stricter entry requirements.

policies.policy_title: Increase police presence and efficiency on the beat
policies.stated: Reform UK will ensure police return to the beat, utilise better technology, reduce paperwork, and allow PCSOs to become police officers before phasing out the role.

source.quote: More Bobbies on the Beat Ensure that police return to the beat and use better technology and stop wasting time on paperwork. Allow PCSOs to become police officers before the role is phased out.

policies.policy_title: End 'woke' policing and reform police oversight
policies.stated: Reform UK will scrap all Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) roles and regulations to stop 'two-tier policing' and overhaul the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) to make the police complaints system more accountable to the public.

source.quote: Common Sense Policing not ‘Woke’ Policing Scrap all Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) roles and regulations to stop two-tier policing. Overhaul the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) so that the police complaints system becomes more accountable and works for the law-abiding public.

policies.policy_title: Build 10,000 new detention places and expand prison capacity
policies.stated: Reform UK will start building 10,000 new state-built and managed detention places and expand prison capacity, commissioning disused military bases if needed, to ensure 'life means life' for those who endanger the public.

source.quote: Start Building of 10,000 New Detention Places Start expansion in capacity of state built and managed prisons so that life means life for those who endanger the public. Commission disused military bases if needed.

policies.policy_title: Urgent sentencing review with automatic life imprisonment for repeat violent offenders
policies.stated: Reform UK will launch an urgent sentencing review, introducing mandatory life sentences for those committing second violent or serious offences.

source.quote: Urgent Sentencing Review with Automatic Life Imprisonment for Violent Repeat Offenders Those committing second violent or serious offences will receive mandatory life sentences.

policies.policy_title: Increase criminal justice budget and reopen magistrates' courts
policies.stated: Reform UK will increase the criminal justice budget from £10 billion to £12 billion to ensure more high-calibre staff and cut delays, and reopen local magistrates' courts to clear case backlogs.

source.quote: Increase the Criminal Justice Budget The budget is almost the same as it was 10 years ago. Increase it from £10 billion to £12 billion to ensure more high calibre staff to cut delays. Reopen local magistrates’ courts to clear the case backlog.

policies.policy_title: Change the definition of hate crime
policies.stated: Reform UK will change the definition of hate crime, asserting that the current CPS and police definition has led to systemic bias and that members of the public should not be investigated based on 'any' perceived hate crime.

source.quote: Change the Definition of Hate Crime The CPS and police definition of a hate crime has led to systemic bias. Members of the British public must not be investigated because ‘any’ person ‘perceives’ that a hate crime has been committed.

policies.policy_title: Reform the Child Maintenance Service
policies.stated: Reform UK will launch a special division of the Family Court for maintenance and defaults, mandate 50/50 shared parental care where appropriate, and ensure rights of access for grandparents.

source.quote: Reform the Child Maintenance Service We will launch a special division of the Family Court for maintenance and defaults. Share parental care 50/50 where appropriate. Rights of access for grandparents.

policies.policy_title: Stop child grooming gangs
policies.stated: Reform UK will deport offenders holding dual citizenship, make child grooming an aggravating offence, improve safeguarding of victims, and deny bail for grooming gang offenders.

source.quote: Stop Child Grooming Gangs Deport offenders holding dual citizenship. Make child grooming an aggravating offence. Improve safeguarding of victims and vulnerable. No bail for grooming gang offenders.

policies.policy_title: Tackle youth crime with High Intensity Training Camps
policies.stated: Reform UK will tackle youth crime by reopening High Intensity Training Camps for young offenders to teach basic education, teamwork, and values.

source.quote: Tackle Youth Crime Reopen High Intensity Training Camps for young offenders to teach basic education, teamwork and values.

policies.policy_title: Implement a patriotic curriculum
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce a patriotic curriculum in primary and secondary schools, reviewing history and social science curricula to ensure balance by pairing any teaching of British or European imperialism/slavery with non-European occurrences.

source.quote: A Patriotic Curriculum in Primary and Secondary Schools Any teaching about a period or example of British or European imperialism or slavery must be paired with the teaching of a non-European occurrence of the same to ensure balance. History and social science curriculum to be reviewed and audited regularly to ensure balance. Our children must be taught about their heritage.

policies.policy_title: Ban transgender ideology in schools and mandate single-sex facilities
policies.stated: Reform UK will ban transgender ideology, including gender questioning, social transitioning, or pronoun swapping, in primary and secondary schools. They will require schools to have single-sex facilities and inform parents of under-16s about their children's life decisions.

source.quote: Ban Transgender Ideology in Primary and Secondary Schools No gender questioning, social transitioning or pronoun swapping. Inform parents of under 16s about their children’s life decisions. Schools must have single sex facilities.

policies.policy_title: Provide tax relief for independent education
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce 20% tax relief on all independent education and abolish VAT on fees, aiming to incentivise parents to choose independent schools and ease pressure on state schools.

source.quote: Tax relief of 20% on all Independent Education No VAT on Fees. If parents can afford to pay a bit more, we should incentivise them to choose independent schools. This will significantly ease pressure on state schools and improve education for all.

policies.policy_title: Reform student loans and university admissions
policies.stated: Reform UK will scrap interest on student loans, extend loan capital repayment periods to 45 years, restrict undergraduate numbers, and enforce minimum entry standards for universities.

source.quote: Scrap Interest on Student Loans Extend loan capital repayment periods to 45 years. Restrict undergraduate numbers well below current levels, too many courses are not good enough and students are being ripped off. Enforce minimum entry standards.

policies.policy_title: Cut funding to universities that undermine free speech
policies.stated: Reform UK will cut funding to universities that undermine free speech, allowing political bias or 'cancel culture' to face heavy financial penalties, as they view the government's Free Speech Act as 'toothless'.

source.quote: Cut Funding to Universities that Undermine Free Speech The government’s Free Speech Act is toothless. Allowing political bias or cancel culture must face heavy financial penalties.

policies.policy_title: Increase permanent exclusions and double Pupil Referral Units
policies.stated: Reform UK will implement permanent exclusions for violent and disruptive students and double the number of Pupil Referral Units (PRUs) to ensure schools can function safely and spread best practice.

source.quote: Permanent Exclusions for Violent and Disruptive Students We will double the number of Pupil Referral Units (PRUs) so schools can function safely. We will also ensure that best practice is spread across PRUs.

policies.policy_title: Introduce 2-year undergraduate courses
policies.stated: Reform UK will mandate that universities provide the option of 2-year undergraduate courses to reduce student debt and allow earlier entry into employment.

source.quote: Universities Must Provide 2-Year Undergraduate Courses The option of 2-year courses would reduce student debt and allow earlier entry into employment to help pay it off.

policies.policy_title: Enforce a 2-strike rule for job offers for benefit claimants
policies.stated: Reform UK will enforce a 2-strike rule where all job seekers and those fit to work must find employment within four months or accept a job after two offers, otherwise, benefits will be withdrawn.

source.quote: Enforce a 2-Strike Rule for Job Offers All job seekers and those fit to work must find employment within 4 months or accept a job after 2 offers. Otherwise, benefits are withdrawn.

policies.policy_title: Require face-to-face assessments for benefits
policies.stated: Reform UK will require Personal Independence Payment and Work Capability Assessments to be face-to-face, with independent medical assessments to prove eligibility. Those with severe disabilities or serious long-term illnesses would be exempt from regular checks.

source.quote: Face to Face, Not Remote Assessments for Benefits Personal Independence Payment and Work Capability Assessment should be face to face. We will require independent medical assessments to prove eligibility for payments. Those registered with severe disabilities or serious long-term illnesses would be exempt from regular checks.

policies.policy_title: Motivate 2 million people back to work
policies.stated: Reform UK will motivate up to 2 million people back to work through reforms to benefit support and training, with a particular focus on 16-34 year olds, and offer tax relief for businesses undertaking apprenticeships.

source.quote: Motivate up to 2 million People Back to Work Reforms to benefit support and training will help people back into work. Particular focus on 16-34 year olds. Employment is critical to improving mental health. Tax relief for businesses that undertake apprenticeships.

policies.policy_title: Scrap EU regulations
policies.stated: Reform UK will legislate to scrap over 6,700 retained EU laws with immediate effect, including those on State Aid, Competition, Employment, Net Zero, and the Environment, which they claim are still based on EU regulations.

source.quote: Legislate to Scrap EU Regulations with Immediate Effect Britain still has over 6,700 retained EU laws, which we will rescind. British laws on State Aid, Competition, Employment, Net Zero and the Environment are still based on EU regulations.

policies.policy_title: Abandon the Windsor Framework
policies.stated: Reform UK will abandon the Windsor Framework, arguing it is worse than the original Northern Ireland Protocol, has partitioned the UK, and means British citizens in Northern Ireland are ruled by EU laws.

source.quote: Abandon the Windsor Framework This is worse than the original Northern Ireland Protocol. The UK has been partitioned down the Irish Sea. Northern Ireland is still in the EU’s single market for goods. It is unacceptable that British citizens in Northern Ireland are being ruled by EU laws.

policies.policy_title: Ensure independence for Britain's Armed Forces from EU programmes
policies.stated: Reform UK will ensure the independence of Britain's Armed Forces from EU programmes, withdrawing from the EU Horizon programme, the European Defence Fund, and the EU’s military mobility project, to prevent them being 'sucked into an EU Command and Control Force'.

source.quote: Independence for Britain’s Armed Forces The government has signed up to the EU Horizon programme. That means we send money to the European Defence Fund and part of the EU’s military mobility project. Our Armed Forces are at risk of being sucked into an EU Command and Control Force.

policies.policy_title: Prepare for renegotiations on the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement
policies.stated: Reform UK will prepare for renegotiations on the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement, stating that a 'level playing field' is holding Britain back.

source.quote: Prepare for Renegotiations on the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement A so-called EU ‘level playing field’ is holding us back.

policies.policy_title: Increase defence spending to 3% of GDP
policies.stated: Reform UK will increase defence spending to 2.5% of national GDP by year three, then to 3% within six years, to increase the size and capacity of the armed forces, improve equipment, quality of life for personnel, and boost morale.

source.quote: Increase Defence Spending to 2.5% of National GDP by year 3, then 3% within 6 years This will increase the size and capacity of our armed forces and ensure our lead role in NATO. It will also improve equipment, quality of life for services personnel and boost morale in military communities.

policies.policy_title: Introduce urgent pay review for armed forces
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce an urgent pay review to increase basic pay across the armed forces to boost recruitment and retention, stating that a private soldier is paid less than an Amazon worker.

source.quote: Introduce Urgent Pay Review Increase basic pay across our armed forces to boost recruitment and retention. It is unacceptable that a private soldier is paid less than an Amazon worker.

policies.policy_title: Introduce new Armed Forces Justice Bill
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce a new Armed Forces Justice Bill to protect service personnel on active duty from civil law and human rights lawyers, and create an armed forces watchdog to fast-track complaints and appeals in housing and welfare.

source.quote: Introduce new Armed Forces Justice Bill Protect our servicemen and women on active duty inside and outside the UK from civil law and human rights lawyers. The bill will also create an armed forces watchdog to fast-track complaints and appeals in housing and welfare.

policies.policy_title: Recruit 30,000 for the army
policies.stated: Reform UK will recruit 30,000 full-time personnel for the army, stating that military national service for young people is not the answer.

source.quote: Recruit 30,000 for the army Military national service for 30,000 young people for one year is not the answer. We need to recruit 30,000 to join the army full time

policies.policy_title: Regenerate Britain's defence manufacturing and technology
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce incentives and tax breaks to boost the UK defence industry, improve equipment self-sufficiency, and manufacture world-class products for export.

source.quote: Regenerate Britain’s Defence Manufacturing and Technology Introduce incentives and tax breaks to boost the UK defence industry. Improve equipment selfsufficiency and manufacture world class products for export.

policies.policy_title: Reform defence procurement
policies.stated: Reform UK will launch a Joint Acquisition Corp to ensure world-class defence procurement, listening to soldiers on the front line to ensure they receive the equipment needed.

source.quote: Reform Defence Procurement Launch a Joint Acquisition Corp to ensure world class procurement. The Ministry of Defence must listen to soldiers on the front line and ensure they get the equipment they need.

policies.policy_title: Provide free education for military personnel
policies.stated: Reform UK will provide free education for military personnel both during and after service, which they deem vital for a successful return to civilian life.

source.quote: Education for Military Personnel Free education both during and after service is vital to ensure a successful return to civilian life.

policies.policy_title: Abolish the Renters' (Reform) Bill
policies.stated: Reform UK will abolish the Renters' (Reform) Bill, stating that existing legislation was inadequate and will instead boost the monitoring, appeals, and enforcement processes for renters with grievances. They will also scrap Section 24 for landlords to encourage smaller landlords into the rental market.

source.quote: Abolish the Renters’ (Reform) Bill Existing legislation was inadequate to address bad practices. Instead, we will boost the monitoring, appeals and enforcement process for renters with grievances. Scrap section 24 for Landlords The tax system should encourage smaller landlords into the rental markets. Not penalise them. We will restore landlords’ rights to deduct finance costs and mortgage interest from tax on rental income.

policies.policy_title: Reform social housing law to prioritise local people
policies.stated: Reform UK will reform social housing law to prioritise local people and those who have paid into the system, stating that foreign nationals must go to the back of the queue.

source.quote: Reform Social Housing Law Prioritise local people and those who have paid into the system. Foreign nationals must go to the back of the queue. Not the front.

policies.policy_title: Protect leaseholders and simplify lease extensions
policies.stated: Reform UK will protect leaseholders by requiring all potential charges to be clearly stated and consented to, enforcing Section 106 agreements, and making it cheaper and easier to extend leases to 990 years and buy freeholds.

source.quote: Protection for Leaseholders All potential charges for leasehold or freehold residents must be clearly stated and consented to. Enforce Section 106 agreements. Ensure it is cheaper and easier to extend leases to 990 years and buy freeholds.

policies.policy_title: Incentivise use of new construction technology
policies.stated: Reform UK will incentivise innovation in construction to speed up building through modular construction, digital technology, and building sites that improve efficiency and cut waste.

source.quote: Incentivise Use of New Construction Technology We will incentivise innovation to speed up building: modular construction, digital technology and building sites that improve efficiency and cut waste.

policies.policy_title: Support marriage through the tax system
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce a UK 25% transferable marriage tax allowance as soon as finances allow, meaning no tax on the first £25,000 of income for either spouse, to make work pay and incentivise people back into the workplace.

source.quote: Support Marriage Through the Tax System As soon as finances allow, introduce a UK 25% transferable marriage tax allowance. This would mean no tax on the first £25,000 of income for either spouse. This will help make work pay and incentivise people trapped on benefits back into the workplace.

policies.policy_title: Provide choice for stay-at-home parents
policies.stated: Reform UK will front-load the Child Benefit system for children aged 1-4 to give parents the choice to spend more time with their children.

source.quote: Choice for Stay-at-Home Mums or Dads The majority of mothers would choose to stay at home more if they could. Front-loading the Child Benefit system for children aged 1-4 would give parents the choice to spend more time with their children.

policies.policy_title: Mandate single-sex spaces
policies.stated: Reform UK will mandate that public toilets and changing areas must provide single-sex facilities.

source.quote: Mandate Single Sex Spaces Public toilets and changing areas must provide single sex facilities.

policies.policy_title: Promote child-friendly app restricted smartphones and investigate social media harms
policies.stated: Reform UK will promote child-friendly app restricted smartphones, launch an inquiry into social media harms due to its association with eating disorders, anxiety, depression, suicide, and the child mental health crisis.

source.quote: Promote Child Friendly App Restricted Smartphones Social media is associated with eating disorders, anxiety, depression, suicide and the child mental health crisis. Launch an inquiry into social media harms.

policies.policy_title: Review the Online Safety Bill regarding free speech
policies.stated: Reform UK will review the Online Safety Bill, asserting that social media giants pushing 'baseless transgender ideology and divisive Critical Race theory' should have no role in regulating free speech.

source.quote: Review the Online Safety Bill Social media giants that push baseless transgender ideology and divisive Critical Race theory should have no role in regulating free speech.

policies.policy_title: Scrap HS2
policies.stated: Reform UK will scrap the remainder of the HS2 project, projecting a saving of £25 billion.

source.quote: Scrap HS2 Save £25 billion by scrapping the rest of this bloated vanity project.

policies.policy_title: Stop the 'war on drivers'
policies.stated: Reform UK will legislate to ban ULEZ, Clean Air Zones, and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods, scrap 20 MPH zones (except where safety is critical), and remove bans on petrol and diesel cars and legal requirements for manufacturers to sell electric cars.

source.quote: Stop the War on Drivers Legislate to ban ULEZ Clean Air Zones and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods. Scrapping Net Zero means no more bans on petrol and diesel cars and no legal requirements for manufacturers to sell electric cars. We will keep the speed limit low where safety is critical. Otherwise, 20 MPH zones will be scrapped.

policies.policy_title: Accelerate transport infrastructure development
policies.stated: Reform UK will accelerate transport infrastructure development, focusing on coastal regions, Wales, the North, and the Midlands, and improving existing rail and road links to ensure integrated services.

source.quote: Accelerate Transport Infrastructure Focus on our coastal regions, Wales, the North, and the Midlands. Improve existing rail and road links. Integrated services are critical.

policies.policy_title: New ownership model for critical national infrastructure
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce a new ownership model for critical national infrastructure, bringing 50% of each utility into public ownership and the other 50% owned by UK pension funds, to ensure British taxpayer control and better management. They will also cap standing charges for low users and pensioners.

source.quote: Tighter Regulation and New Ownership Model for Critical National Infrastructure The British taxpayer needs to be in control of Britain’s utilities. Launch a new model that brings 50% of each utility into public ownership. The other 50% would be owned by UK pension funds, benefiting from new expertise and better management. We will ensure standing charges are capped to help low users and pensioners.

policies.policy_title: Streamline infrastructure funding and abolish Net Zero objectives
policies.stated: Reform UK will overhaul and merge the National Infrastructure Commission and the Infrastructure Bank into a single government infrastructure funding stream, simplifying the funding process and abolishing Net Zero objectives to save time, cut waste, and boost funding and accountability.

source.quote: A Single Government Infrastructure Funding Stream Overhaul and merge the National Infrastructure Commission and the Infrastructure Bank. Scrap Net Zero objectives. Simplify the funding process to save time, cut waste, boost funding and accountability.

policies.policy_title: Increase farming budget and focus on smaller farms
policies.stated: Reform UK will increase the farming budget to £3 billion, focusing on smaller farms, keeping farmland in use, bringing young people into farming, boosting the rural economy and culture, and encouraging innovation and diversification.

source.quote: Increase the Farming Budget to £3 Billion Focus on smaller farms. Keep farmland in use. Bring young people into farming. Boost rural economy and culture. Increase innovation and diversification. Help farmers to farm, not pay them to leave or retire.

policies.policy_title: Scrap climate-related farming subsidies and stop Natural England actions damaging farmers
policies.stated: Reform UK will scrap climate-related farming subsidies, replacing current subsidies with direct payments, and stop Natural England from taking actions that damage farmers, ensuring productive land is farmed rather than used for solar farms or rewilding.

source.quote: Scrap Climate-Related Farming Subsidies Productive land must be farmed, not be used for solar farms or rewilding. Replace current subsidies with direct payments. Stop Natural England from taking action that damages farmers.

policies.policy_title: Protect country sports
policies.stated: Reform UK will protect country sports, stating that they increase investment, aid conservation, and boost rural jobs, communities, and local economies.

source.quote: Protect Country Sports These increase investment and help conservation of our environment. They boost rural jobs, communities and local economies.

policies.policy_title: Stop supermarket price fixing and support direct sales for farmers
policies.stated: Reform UK will grant powers to the Competitions and Markets Authority to ensure fair pricing and stop supermarket price fixing. They will also help farmers sell produce directly to the public and change planning laws to support farm shops with zero business rates.

source.quote: Stop Supermarket Price Fixing Grant powers to the Competitions and Markets Authority to ensure fair pricing. Help farmers sell their produce directly to the public. Change planning laws to support farm shops with zero business rates.

policies.policy_title: Prioritise 'Buy British' for food security
policies.stated: Reform UK will target 70% 'Buy British' to ensure food security, mandate taxpayer-funded organisations to source 75% of their food from the UK, implement clear labelling for consumer choice, and boost smaller food processors and abattoirs through tax breaks.

source.quote: Buy British. Buy Quality Target 70% to ensure food security. Taxpayer funded organisations should source 75% of their food from the UK. Clear labelling for consumer choice. Boost smaller food processors and abattoirs through tax breaks and other incentives.

policies.policy_title: Reduce red tape for farmers
policies.stated: Reform UK will cut red tape from HMRC and the British Cattle Movement Service, stating that many farmers spend over 15 hours a week on paperwork.

source.quote: Farming not Form Filling Many farmers spend over 15 hours a week on paperwork. Cut red tape from HMRC and the British Cattle Movement Service.

policies.policy_title: End automatic access for EU fishers to UK waters
policies.stated: Reform UK will end automatic access for EU fishers to UK waters, requiring every foreign fishing vessel to pay for a licence to gain access to the UK's 200 nautical mile Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and stop foreign owners using British flags of convenience.

source.quote: Stop EU Fishers Taking UK Quotas End automatic access to UK waters. Every foreign fishing vessel must pay for a licence to gain access to the UK’s 200 nautical mile Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), as designated under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Stop Foreign Owners using British flags of convenience. Quota reforms needed to help small scale fishing.

policies.policy_title: Expand Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron and assess dedicated coast guard
policies.stated: Reform UK will expand the Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron to police Britain's 200 nautical mile EEZ properly, and assess the possibility of creating a dedicated coast guard or fisheries protection agency.

source.quote: Expand the Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron Police Britain’s 200 nautical mile EEZ properly. Assess the possibility of creating a dedicated coast guard or fisheries protection agency.

policies.policy_title: Ban foreign supertrawlers from UK waters
policies.stated: Reform UK will ban foreign supertrawlers from UK waters, extend the ban on pair trawling for bass beyond the South East and 12-mile territorial waters, and ban Dutch vessels from electric pulse fishing in Britain's 200 mile EEZ.

source.quote: Ban Foreign Supertrawlers from UK Waters Extend the ban on pair trawling for bass beyond the South East and 12-mile territorial waters. Ban Dutch vessels from electric pulse fishing in Britain’s 200 mile EEZ.

policies.policy_title: Rebuild UK fish processing industry
policies.stated: Reform UK will rebuild the UK fish processing industry through tax and other incentives to ensure that all fish caught in British waters are landed and processed in the UK, and by foreign vessels when capacity allows.

source.quote: Rebuild UK Fish Processing Tax and other incentives to ensure that all fish caught in British waters are landed and processed in the UK. Fish caught by foreign vessels in UK waters should also be landed and processed here when capacity allows.

policies.policy_title: Revitalise the UK's fishing fleet
policies.stated: Reform UK will revitalise the UK’s fishing fleet through tax incentives and vocational training, and include fishing communities in policy making.

source.quote: Revitalise the UK’s Fishing Fleet Tax incentives and vocational training to increase UK fishing fleets. Include fishing communities in policy making.

policies.policy_title: Guarantee sustainable fish stocks
policies.stated: Reform UK will guarantee sustainable fish stocks by implementing a 'dynamic management system' and working with national and regional partners such as the North East Atlantic Fisheries Commission.

source.quote: Guarantee Sustainable Stocks Implement a ‘dynamic management system’. Work with national and regional partners such as the North East Atlantic Fisheries Commission.

policies.policy_title: Commence Royal Commission of Inquiry into Social Care
policies.stated: Reform UK will commence a Royal Commission of Inquiry into the social care system to develop a national plan for a sustainable sector, focusing on flexibility, tax incentives, VAT breaks, reduced waste, and a single funding stream. More funding will be provided once a national plan is agreed.

source.quote: Commence Royal Commission of Inquiry into Social Care System A national plan is critical for a sustainable social care system. The sector needs flexibility, tax incentives, VAT breaks and less waste. Simplify social care through a single funding stream, instead of the split between NHS and Local Authorities. More funding will be needed when a national plan is agreed.

policies.policy_title: Stop offshore tax avoidance by care home providers
policies.stated: Reform UK will stop offshore tax avoidance by care home providers, specifically targeting larger providers avoiding tax on profits through complex offshore property company structures and high interest shareholder loans.

source.quote: Stop the Offshore Taxpayer Rip Off Some larger care home providers are avoiding tax on hundreds of millions of profits through complex offshore property company structures and high interest shareholder loans. This has to end.

policies.policy_title: Review pension provision
policies.stated: Reform UK will review pension provision, aiming to simplify the current system, which they describe as complex, costly, and yielding poor returns, by learning from models like Australia.

source.quote: Review Pension Provision The current pension system is riddled with complexity, huge cost and poor returns leading to less uptake. Countries like Australia do savings and pensions much better and cheaper than we have and from a much younger age.

policies.policy_title: End the Mineworkers Pension Scandal
policies.stated: Reform UK will accept in full the Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy Committee 2021 recommendations to amend the Mineworkers Pension Scheme arrangements so that all scheme surpluses accrue to the Mineworkers.

source.quote: End the Mineworkers Pension Scandal We accept the Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy Committee 2021 recommendations in full to amend the Mineworkers Pension Scheme arrangements so that all the scheme surpluses accrue to the Mineworkers.

policies.policy_title: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights and reform the Human Rights Act
policies.stated: Reform UK will leave the European Convention on Human Rights and commence reform of the Human Rights Act to prioritise the rights of law-abiding people.

source.quote: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights Commence reform of the Human Rights Act so that it puts the rights of law-abiding people first.

policies.policy_title: Reform the House of Lords and Civil Service leadership
policies.stated: Reform UK will replace the House of Lords with a smaller, more democratic second chamber, with its structure to be debated and an immediate end to political appointees. They will replace Civil Service leaders with successful professionals from the private sector who are political appointees and come and go with the government.

source.quote: Commence Reform of the House of Lords & Civil Service Replace the crony-filled House of Lords with a much smaller, more democratic second chamber. Structure to be debated. Immediate end of political appointees. Replace Civil Service leaders with successful professionals from the private sector, who are political appointees, who come and go with the government.

policies.policy_title: Reform the postal voting system
policies.stated: Reform UK will reform the postal voting system, stopping postal voting except for the elderly, disabled, or those unable to leave their homes, citing electoral fraud concerns.

source.quote: Commence Reform of the Postal Voting System Postal voting has allowed electoral fraud. We will stop postal voting except for the elderly, disabled or those who can’t leave their homes.

policies.policy_title: Introduce Proportional Representation for the House of Commons
policies.stated: Reform UK will introduce Proportional Representation voting for the House of Commons, stating that large numbers of voters are unrepresented and new parties are shut out, which they believe could increase voter turnout. A referendum is needed for this change.

source.quote: Proportional Representation Voting for the House of Commons Large numbers of voters have no representation in parliament and new parties are shut out of the political system. Voter turnout could be some 10% higher with PR. A referendum is needed.

policies.policy_title: Establish a British Bill of Rights
policies.stated: Reform UK will establish a British Bill of Rights to codify and guarantee freedoms, ensuring the country cannot be locked down on 'shoddy evidence and lies,' and that data/privacy are protected with limited public surveillance and accountability for monitors.

source.quote: A British Bill of Rights Our freedoms must be codified and guaranteed. Never again can our entire country be locked down on shoddy evidence and lies. Our data and privacy must be protected. Surveillance of the public must be limited and those monitoring us held to account.

policies.policy_title: Reaffirm British sovereignty and reject international influence
policies.stated: Reform UK will reaffirm British sovereignty by rejecting the influence of the World Economic Forum, rejecting the World Health Organisation (WHO) Pandemic Treaty, and cancelling WHO membership unless there is fundamental reform. They also oppose the creation of a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) and a cashless society.

source.quote: Reaffirm British Sovereignty Reject the influence of the World Economic Forum. Reject the World Health Organisation (WHO) Pandemic Treaty and cancel our membership of the WHO unless there is fundamental reform to its structure and funding. Reform UK also opposes the Creation of a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). We oppose a cashless society.

policies.policy_title: Replace the 2010 Equalities Act and scrap DE&I rules
policies.stated: Reform UK will replace the 2010 Equalities Act, stating it requires discrimination in the name of 'positive action,' and will scrap Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) rules that they claim have lowered standards and reduced economic productivity.

source.quote: Replace the 2010 Equalities Act The Equalities Act requires discrimination in the name of ‘positive action’. We will scrap Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) rules that have lowered standards and reduced economic productivity.

policies.policy_title: Propose a Comprehensive Free Speech Bill
policies.stated: Reform UK will propose a Comprehensive Free Speech Bill to legislate against 'left-wing bias and politically correct ideology,' addressing 'de-banking, cancel culture, left wing hate mobs or political bias in public institutions,' and stopping Sharia law being used in the UK.

source.quote: Propose a Comprehensive Free Speech Bill Legislate to stop left-wing bias and politically correct ideology that threatens personal freedom and democracy. No more de-banking, cancel culture, left wing hate mobs or political bias in public institutions. Stop Sharia law being used in the UK.

policies.policy_title: Reform the BBC and scrap the TV licence
policies.stated: Reform UK will reform the BBC, describing it as 'out-of-touch, wasteful, and institutionally biased,' and will scrap the TV licence, arguing that people should be free to choose in a world of on-demand TV.

source.quote: Commence Reform of the BBC The out-of-touch wasteful BBC is institutionally biased. The TV licence is taxation without representation. We will scrap it. In a world of on-demand TV People should be free to choose.

policies.policy_title: Make St George's and St David's Day public holidays
policies.stated: Reform UK will make St George’s and St David’s Day public holidays, stating that English national identity should be officially promoted and celebrated.

source.quote: Make St George’s and St David’s Day a Public Holiday English national identity should be officially promoted and celebrated, not ignored or banned.

policies.policy_title: Launch an Anti-Corruption Unit for Westminster
policies.stated: Reform UK will launch a new Anti-Corruption Unit for Westminster with legal powers to investigate past and future scandals, ensuring public officials face sanctions, including prison, if they break the rules.

source.quote: Launch an Anti-Corruption Unit for Westminster We will ensure that public officials face sanctions if they break the rules, including prison. Our new Anti-Corruption Unit will have legal powers to investigate past and future scandals.

normalization_note: Consolidated 'Reform the planning system to fast-track housing and infrastructure on brownfield sites' and 'Review the planning system for brownfield development' as they both detail fast-tracking brownfield housing development. All other policies were distinct at the material-policy standard and their outcomes were re-tagged for strict alignment with the provided fundamentals taxonomy, ensuring single or maximum two direct outcomes per policy where plausible.
